overview.title: Agadir’s big everyday market
overview.p1: Souk El Had is where Agadir shops for real life: fruit, vegetables, spices, olives, clothes and household goods. It is less touristic than medina souks in imperial cities, and more about volume and local prices.
overview.p2: Go in the morning for the freshest produce and cooler air. Bargain politely on non-food items; fixed-price stalls exist too. Keep valuables close in crowded aisles.

food.title: Eat near the souk
food.p1: Simple grills and juice stalls sit around the market edges — good for a quick bite after browsing.
food.li3: Café stops on the outer streets.
food.li4: Wash fruit if you buy produce.

1.title: Getting there
1.desc: Petit taxi from the beach or centre; ask for Souk El Had.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Mornings are best. Some sections slow in the afternoon heat.

3.title: Shopping
3.desc: Compare prices on spices and crafts; polite bargaining is normal.

q1.question: Is Souk El Had open every day?
q1.answer: Much of the market operates daily, with peak activity in the morning. Some sections are busier on traditional market days.

q2.question: Is it touristy?
q2.answer: Less than medina souks in Marrakech or Fes — many stalls serve local shoppers.

q3.question: What should I buy?
q3.answer: Spices, olives, argan products, simple textiles and fresh produce if you have a kitchen.

q4.question: Do I need a guide?
q4.answer: No — the layout is large but navigable. A guide can help if you want product explanations.

q5.question: How long do I need?
q5.answer: One to two hours is enough for most visitors.
